accessibility: Both fields are required and labelled; an error is a line of text under the field (with an icon), never color alone, and focus moves to the first problem after a refused creation.
The dialog has a title and a description, a visible close control, and keeps a visible 2px primary focus outline on every control.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Panel dialog, Stack, Text, Icon, TextInput, Select, SelectOption, Button, Alert); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The View names listed are baked samples of the dogfood Workspace's Views, and the typed name is a literal; the refused-creation sentence is one catalog sentence of the server's diagnostics, standing for the real one.
The View list of the app has a Find field and a check beside the chosen View, which the Select Widget does not draw.

A Select list is drawn inside the dialog and would be clipped by it, so a Variant that opens one also shows a blank spacer at the end of the dialog to give the list room; the app's list floats over the page.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (View names, the typed name); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A holder of flows.write on a desktop layout pressed New Flow on the UX Flows page, or on the empty state of a Workspace with no Flows (/flows); the dialog is not offered on a tablet or phone layout.

The base state is the freshly opened dialog: an empty name and the View last opened (or the first View) chosen for the entry step; Variants type a name, open the View list, show each refusal and the creating and failed states.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the dialog is centered over a dimmed ground.
spec.intent: Show the New Flow dialog of the UX Flows page as built from Adapter Widgets only: a name and the View that the entry step opens, which are all the Workbench needs to create a Flow.
interactionRules: A Flow needs a name and one View: an empty name and a missing View are each refused before anything is sent, each with a line of text under its field.
Create Flow makes the Flow with one entry step on the chosen View, in its base state and without transitions, and is busy while it works; on success the dialog closes and the page opens the new Flow.
A refused creation shows its reason in an alert inside the dialog and keeps the typed name; with no Views the View field says a View is needed first.

references.label: Phase 5 of the closed loop: dogfood coverage of the core surfaces
